questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses at the university aligned with my academic interests, I liked the city and I wanted to improve my German

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay. The registration process for the courses was very confusing and it would have been difficult for me to figure out the system without the help from local students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were a welcoming event when they provided a lot of information

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got it through the university, which was just based on luck. Otherwise it would likely have been difficult for me to find housing

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is not a problem, there's a looot of public transportation

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration was quite easy, you just have to pay the semester fee, fill out a document and show proof of insurance.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The reply on e-mail was a bit slow, but I think it was because I contacted them in september and the semester does not start until mid october

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The system is very confusing. So apparantly everyone applies for at lot of courses, and then gets rejected to most (I got rejected for all of my courses, which was a bit stressful when you dont know that it's normal procedure), and then you just physically attend the courses you want and then the professor will most likely allow you on the course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Maybe to just relax a bit, cause you will probably get the courses you want, they are just very chill about the registration, you don't apply in advance, you just figure it out as the courses are starting.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think it was fine. The system is quite different from the way the biology courses are structured at KU. So there's both a practical, lecture and seminar part, and the practical part and seminar part can be quite demanding, as the practical requires long, intense days, and the seminar can be a lot of work as you have to conduct a 30 min seminar. At least that was the structure of the courses that I attended in the biology faculty.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The structure as I mentioned above. The teacher-student relationship also required some getting used to on my part.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Biodiversity and Evolution 1 (Theory)
Soil Ecosystems as Biodiversity Hot Spot
Cognition, Evolution and Behaviour

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Biodiversity and Evolution was a fun course, and did not have a practical part actually. It involved a lot of different teachers with many different academic background which was very interesting. 
Soil Ecosystems as Biodiversity Hot Spot turned out to be a very interesting course even though I am not normally that interested in soil ecosystems, but it was interesting. 
Cognition, Evolution and Behaviour was a quite intense course with long days during the practical part. You get to get some experience with experimental animals and you conduct an animal experiment as well.

questions.answer: Semester fee, but then you also get a student card which gives you free transportation, so I was not sure if I should put that amount (1.980,00 DKK) in the transportation box.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It is much cheaper than Denmark, but I expected it to be. You can live very cheap if you want

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a long list of sport activities quite cheap through the university, I also have a friend who got free instrument lessons

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: there's a possibility to do whatever you want, so I would recommend to try out a lot of things. you can also attend classes a single time

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: there is a lot of museums, museums are free on the first sunday of every month. Then there a lot of cultural activities going on every weekend and day.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy as german and danish culture are similar and most germans in berlin are good at english

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: attend the HUGS attend

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: sometimes the germans forget to smile :) and public transportation can be a bit chaotic

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It is very relaxed, lots of opportunities, very free and non-judging atmosphere

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: do the language course on HU, I did not do that and I regret is as it was a very good social opportunity. Take your time finding a good place, consider the dorms as they are cheaper and then you'll have more money for fun stuff, and transportation takes a while no matter where you live, so it's not a problem if you dont live very central. And just dont stress to much about the way the administration works, cause they dont, it will all work out.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to understand the course registration at your faculty, maybe contact some students who went to the same as you're going to, that will be a big stress relief I think.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing a different culture and another university.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Gaining the energy for some of the more intense parts of my courses while establishing social life and navigating in a new country

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
